title: Weak or congested growth — what to do once confirmed

common.preserved_uncertainty: The number of canes to keep varies by source and region, from 1–4 to 4–8 (C-2), so Pip gives a range. The sunscald caution comes from one source and applies to hot-summer climates (AF-18). The one-third caution comes from general (not rose-specific) advice about annual crown removal (AF-18). No source explains why weak canes should be removed before congestion is decided; the order follows how sources sequence the work (AF-14; U-6).

decision_notes.text: Weak cane: remove it completely, at its base or where it starts. Don't shorten it.
Crowded bush: remove whole canes, never part-shorten one. Keep the strongest, then aim for even spacing and an open, airy centre.
Keep roughly 3–7 strong canes, 4–6 typical, and fewer for a modest or young plant.
If the plant already looks weak or small, prune it lightly.
In hot-summer areas, leave some growth in the middle to shade the graft. Don't clear all the crowding at once.
Reaching inside the bush, wear eye protection and long-cuffed gloves.
